name: Call of Water
summary: Brine sends shamans into the Barrens to gather water for a sapta. The trial begins with a sample from the guarded pool below her hill, where water means survival.

sections.title: A Lesson in the Desert
sections.body: Brine asks shaman initiates to study water in all its forms before she grants the water sapta that lets them commune with the spirits. In the arid Barrens, water means the difference between survival and starvation. She asks them to notice what water makes possible: forests flourish where it flows, deserts starve where it is absent, and living beings will kill to protect even the humblest spring.

sections.title: The Quilboar's Hoard
sections.body: Native quilboar fiercely guard the watering hole beneath Brine's hill. They treat every pool as a priceless hoard and feast whenever rain comes. Brine regrets the violence their hoarding brings, but their insular greed and divided clans keep their threat contained. For the other races surviving on the plains, that leaves a precarious balance.

faq.q: What is the purpose of collecting water for Brine?
faq.answer: Brine needs samples of pure water from distinct corners of the world to brew a ceremonial water sapta. The draught opens an initiate's perception, allowing communion with elemental water spirits.

faq.q: Why is the watering hole below Brine so heavily contested?
faq.answer: In the parched Barrens, water is the most precious resource. Local quilboar treat every pool as sacred treasure and fight fiercely against anyone who tries to draw from it.
Brine is an orc shaman and hermit who lives in a lonely hut overlooking the southern Barrens. Her deep wisdom about water and elemental spirits guides Horde shamans toward communion.

faq.q: What happens after returning the filled brown waterskin?
faq.answer: After you return with a sample from the watering hole, Brine sends you farther afield to gather pristine water from very different places, including the well of Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills.

faq.q: Why does Brine remark on the quilboar's division?
faq.answer: Brine sees the quilboar's territorial ways and clan rivalries as causes of their misery. If they united instead of fighting over isolated springs, they would threaten the rest of the Barrens far more.

A sapta is a mystical elixir shamans prepare from gathered reagents and waters aligned with the elements. Drinking it expands spiritual sight, revealing elemental beings usually hidden from mortal eyes.

angles.text: As a shaman, you learn that water brings healing and restoration, but also sparks conflict and the desperate struggle to survive.
As a member of the Horde, you face the challenge of controlling and sharing water in the Barrens, where tribes and beasts constantly fight over every trickle.
